newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait stock index eases slightly in record week.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait stock index eases slightly in record week.

text.p: Kuwait share index soared 75 points to 2,139.2 in the week to Wednesday, but eased slightly from a new record reached on Tuesday.
"It was a good week...coming weeks will be (even) better, God willing," said Mohammad al-Duhaishi, a private dealer.
The index broke through the 2,100 mark on Monday and closed at 2,144.7 on Tuesday before easing slightly on Wednesday.

Traders say the index, which closed on Wednesday 12.3 percent higher from the start of 1997, has been gaining on the back of strong year-end results by listed companies which are still being issued. It rose about 40 percent in 1996.
"Most of the company profits were very good and we expect some other companies to announce good profits taking their shares up," added Duhaishi.
Gainers led losers 34-15 this week while 11 were non-movers, figures released by the Kuwait Stock Exchange on Thursday show.
The daily average of traded value almost doubled this week to 51.4 million dinars ($170 million). Volume rose to a daily average of 166.8 million shares from 97.7 million.

The upward trend was also fueled by remarks by Kuwaiti Crown Prince Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah who told a local daily that the security situation was stable although he reiterated warnings about intentions by former occupier Iraq, said one dealer of the "reassuring" statement.
Investment firms dominated activity this week with a traded value of 134.7 million dinars, followed by banks with 45.7 million and property firms with 35.3 million.
Commercial Bank, Gulf Bank, Kuwait Investment, International Investor, Securities House, National Investment and National Real Estate were among the most active shares.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest in mutual funds.
